- First orbital camera platforms deployed above Earth reveal blank continents hidden beyond Atlantic mists, shattering centuries of cartographic ignorance.

* 1905 – First Contact
- Aerial reconnaissance teams spot dense indigenous settlements, sprawling agricultural networks, and towering stone cities across the newly visible landmass.

* 1907 – Cultural Shock
- Global governments scramble as millions of previously unknown civilizations demand recognition, treaties, and territorial sovereignty under newly established international law.

- Representatives from forty-seven previously isolated nations convene aboard floating platforms in the Caribbean, drafting the Atlantic Accord to prevent colonial exploitation.

* 1920 – Integration Era
- Trade routes explode as indigenous technologies—advanced metallurgy, living architecture, and bioengineered agriculture—transform European and Asian economies overnight.

* 1935 – The Unification
- A pancontinental government forms, merging old-world parliaments with indigenous council systems into a single governing body headquartered on floating islands.
